initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden catastrophic anterior chest pain tearing through to the upper back
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Sudden onset 45 minutes prior to ED arrival

releasedFindings: Significant 46 mmHg systolic blood pressure differential between right arm (188/104) and left arm (142/86).
Diminished left radial and femoral pulses.
New high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur heard best along the right sternal border (acute aortic regurgitation).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Sudden tearing pain with pulse deficit and acute aortic regurgitation murmur establishes presumptive acute Stanford Type A aortic dissection; immediate contraindication to anticoagulation or antiplatelets.

releasedFindings: Urgent portable CXR reveals marked mediastinal widening (> 8 cm) and abnormal aortic knob contour.
ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia with non-specific ST-T changes (excludes focal STEMI).

Emergent ECG-gated CT Angiography (CTA) of chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrates intimal flap originating 1.2 cm above the sinotubular junction extending through the aortic arch into the descending thoracic aorta.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirmed Stanford Type A / DeBakey Type I aortic dissection; initiate urgent IV beta-blockade (Esmolol) targeting SBP 100-120 mmHg and HR < 60 bpm, followed by vasodilator if needed, with immediate emergent cardiothoracic surgery mobilization.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Stanford Type A (DeBakey Type I) Aortic Dissection
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Sudden maximal tearing chest and back pain, pulse deficit, unequal upper extremity blood pressures, acute aortic regurgitation murmur, widened mediastinum, and CTA demonstrating ascending aortic intimal flap.

clinicalScores.formula: High-risk conditions (1) + High-risk pain features (1) + High-risk exam findings (1)
requiredInputs: Pulse deficit or BP differential > 20 mmHg
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Assign points only for verified high-risk categories.

expectedInvestigations.testName: ECG-gated CT Angiography of Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Definitive gold-standard for diagnosing aortic dissection, entry tear, and visceral malperfusion.
Differentiate from STEMI and evaluate for RCA involvement / inferior ischemia.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Type and Crossmatch 6 Units PRBCs, FFP, Platelets
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Immediate surgical preparation for emergent cardiopulmonary bypass.

immediateInterventions: IV Esmolol infusion titrated to HR < 60 bpm prior to vasodilator
IV Nitroprusside or Nicardipine if SBP remains > 120 mmHg after beta-blockade
Adequate IV opioid analgesia (Fentanyl) to blunt sympathetic surge
definitiveTherapy: Emergent open surgical repair with ascending aortic graft replacement and valve resuspension/replacement

highRiskInteractions: Giving hydralazine or nitroprusside alone causes reflex tachycardia and accelerates aortic rupture.

criticalFailures.description: Administering heparin or thrombolytic for suspected ACS without ruling out aortic dissection

guidelineReferences.organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association
guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe acute respiratory distress 48 hours following an unwitnessed aspiration event
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive tachypnea and hypoxia over past 24 hours

releasedFindings: ABG on 100% Non-Rebreather: pH 7.28, PaCO2 48 mmHg, PaO2 54 mmHg, HCO3 22 mmol/L.
Patient is intubated: post-intubation PaO2 is 62 mmHg on FiO2 1.0 with PEEP 10 cmH2O (PaO2/FiO2 ratio = 62 mmHg).
Portable CXR: Diffuse, bilateral fluffy alveolar opacities sparing the costophrenic angles.

Bedside echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (60%), normal left atrial size, no regional wall motion abnormalities, IVC collapsibility 40% (rules out cardiogenic pulmonary edema).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Meets Berlin definition for Severe ARDS (P/F ratio < 100 mmHg on PEEP >= 5 cmH2O within 7 days of acute insult with non-cardiogenic bilateral infiltrates).

releasedFindings: Patient weight: 70 kg, predicted body weight (PBW): 52 kg.
Initial ventilator set to tidal volume 500 mL (9.6 mL/kg PBW), resulting in plateau pressure (Pplat) 36 cmH2O and driving pressure 24 cmH2O.
Hypoxia persists despite neuromuscular blockade infusion.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Immediate reduction of tidal volume to ARDSNet protocol (4-6 mL/kg PBW, target 310 mL) to lower Pplat < 30 cmH2O and driving pressure < 15 cmH2O; mandatory initiation of prone positioning for >= 16 hours/day (PROSEVA trial).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) secondary to aspiration pneumonitis
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Meets Berlin Definition for Severe ARDS: Acute onset within 1 week of clinical insult, bilateral infiltrates on chest imaging not fully explained by cardiac failure, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio = 62 mmHg (< 100 mmHg) with PEEP >= 5 cmH2O.

rankedDifferential.condition: Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema / Flash Pulmonary Edema

clinicalScores.formula: PaO2 / FiO2 ratio on PEEP >= 5 cmH2O
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Cannot grade ARDS severity without arterial blood gas and exact ventilator FiO2 and PEEP.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess PaO2, oxygenation ratio, and acute respiratory acidosis.
Exclude cardiogenic etiology and evaluate right ventricular strain / cor pulmonale.

immediateInterventions: Low tidal volume ventilation: 4-6 mL/kg predicted body weight (310 mL)
Maintain plateau pressure Pplat <= 30 cmH2O and driving pressure <= 14 cmH2O
Early prone positioning for at least 16 consecutive hours daily
definitiveTherapy: Conservative fluid management after shock resolution
Evaluation for VV-ECMO if P/F < 80 mmHg persists

strictContraindications: High tidal volume ventilation (> 8 mL/kg PBW)
Excessive fluid boluses without hemodynamic responsiveness
Supine-only positioning in refractory severe ARDS
highRiskInteractions: Over-ventilation with large tidal volumes induces barotrauma and ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI).

criticalFailures.description: Failing to adopt low-tidal-volume lung-protective ventilation in severe ARDS

mandatoryActions: Reduce tidal volume to 4-6 mL/kg PBW

guidelineReferences.organization: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine
guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: ESICM Guidelines on Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome 2023

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden acute vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and bilateral lower extremity weakness
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Witnessed acute onset 3 hours ago while eating lunch

releasedFindings: Neurologic exam: Skew deviation, bilateral horizontal and vertical nystagmus, bilateral cranial nerve VI and VII palsies, and bilateral Babinski signs.
NIHSS is 18.
Patient exhibits rapid fluctuation into somnolence, with bilateral pin-point pupils (pons localization).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Classic 'top of the basilar' / basilar artery occlusion syndrome; devastating high-mortality ischemic emergency requiring immediate neurovascular imaging and thrombectomy activation.

releasedFindings: Non-contrast Head CT: No intracranial hemorrhage; subtle early hypoattenuation in the ventral pons; pc-ASPECTS score 8.
CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck: Complete flow void / occlusion of the mid-to-distal basilar artery.
CT Perfusion: Preserved penumbra throughout posterior cerebral artery territories.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Basilar artery occlusion confirmed; patient is within the 0-24 hour window for emergent mechanical thrombectomy (ATTENTION / BAOCHE trials); administer IV tenecteplase/alteplase if within 4.5h and rapidly mobilize neurointerventional team to cath lab.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion (Posterior Circulation Ischemic Stroke)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Acute brainstem and cerebellar ischemic syndrome manifesting as vertigo, cranial nerve palsies, dysarthria, fluctuating somnolence, and pin-point pupils, confirmed by CTA demonstrating basilar artery occlusion.

clinicalScores.formula: 10-point scale evaluating midbrain (2), pons (2), thalamus (2), occipital cortex (2), cerebellum (2)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires non-contrast CT assessment of posterior fossa structures.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Non-Contrast Head CT and CT Angiography Head & Neck
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Rule out hemorrhage and confirm site of basilar occlusion.

immediateInterventions: Immediate emergency activation of Endovascular Thrombectomy (EVT) team
IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg if within 4.5 hours and no contraindications
Airway protection / intubation if GCS drops or bulbar compromise worsens
definitiveTherapy: Mechanical thrombectomy (aspiration / stent retriever) within 24 hours of onset

strictContraindications: Acute blood pressure lowering (SBP < 140 mmHg) in un-recanalized basilar occlusion
Delaying EVT team mobilization to observe IV thrombolytic response
highRiskInteractions: Iatrogenic hypotension collapses collateral flow through the circle of Willis and causes irreversible brainstem death.

criticalFailures.description: Dismissing posterior circulation stroke as benign peripheral vertigo or delaying EVT mobilization

requiredKeyFindings: Brainstem signs (pin-point pupils, cranial nerve palsies)

guidelineReferences.organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: 2023 AHA/ASA Focused Update on Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke

pastMedicalHistory: Splenectomy at age 8 following motor vehicle crash

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe explosive headache, photophobia, fever, and confusion

releasedFindings: Physical exam: Inability to touch chin to chest (severe nuchal rigidity), positive Kernig sign and positive Brudzinski sign.
Rapidly spreading non-blanching purpuric and petechial lesions over both thighs and trunk (purpura fulminans).
Patient is disoriented to time and place (GCS 13).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Suspected acute bacterial meningitis, likely Neisseria meningitidis or Streptococcus pneumoniae in an asplenic patient with septic shock and purpura fulminans; requires immediate empiric antibiotics and steroids within minutes.

releasedFindings: Serum WBC: 28,400/uL with 22% band forms; platelets 78,000/uL.
Serum Lactate: 5.2 mmol/L; INR 1.9.
CT Head is requested by nursing prior to lumbar puncture.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: CRITICAL SAFETY GATE: Never delay antimicrobial administration for imaging or lumbar puncture. Draw 2 blood cultures immediately, administer IV Ceftriaxone 2g + Vancomycin + Dexamethasone 10mg IV immediately (within 30 minutes); perform head CT and LP only after antibiotic infusion.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Fulminant Meningococcal Meningitis with Septic Shock and Purpura Fulminans
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Classic triad of fever, altered mental status, and nuchal rigidity in a college student with asplenia, accompanied by purpura fulminans and septic shock.

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Bacterial Meningitis (Neisseria meningitidis / Streptococcus pneumoniae)

clinicalScores.formula: RR >= 22 (1) + SBP <= 100 (1) + Altered mental status GCS < 15 (1)
clinicalScores.expectedResult: High Risk for In-Hospital Sepsis Mortality (Score = 3)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires all three clinical vitals/mental status parameters.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Blood Cultures (2 sets) prior to antibiotics without delay
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Isolate pathogen prior to antibiotic sterilization of blood.
CSF cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain, and PCR.

immediateInterventions: IV Dexamethasone 10mg immediately prior to or with first dose of antibiotics
Empiric IV Ceftriaxone 2g + Vancomycin 15-20 mg/kg within 30 minutes of arrival
Fluid resuscitation with 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloids for septic shock
definitiveTherapy: Targeted parenteral antibiotics tailored to CSF culture and antimicrobial susceptibility
Public health chemoprophylaxis for close contacts

strictContraindications: Delaying antimicrobial administration for CT imaging or lumbar puncture
Administering steroids hours after antibiotics have been started
highRiskInteractions: Every hour of delay in antibiotic administration for bacterial meningitis increases mortality by up to 12%.

criticalFailures.description: Delaying empiric antibiotics to obtain a head CT scan or perform lumbar puncture in acute bacterial meningitis

mandatoryActions: Antibiotics and dexamethasone immediately without delay for CT/LP

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Found down on the floor for approximately 18 hours after a fall; severe bilateral thigh pain
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Found by neighbor this morning; unable to rise from floor

releasedFindings: Urinalysis dipstick: 3+ Blood; Microscopic urinalysis: 0-1 RBC/hpf (classic myoglobinuria pigment dissociation).
Serum Creatine Kinase (CK): 78,500 U/L (massive rhabdomyolysis).
Serum Potassium: 6.6 mmol/L with peaked, narrow T waves on 12-lead ECG.
Serum Creatinine: 3.8 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL) with BUN 64 mg/dL.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Severe rhabdomyolysis with pigment-induced acute tubular necrosis (ATN) and life-threatening hyperkalemia with ECG changes; emergent membrane stabilization with IV calcium gluconate followed by shifting and high-volume fluid resuscitation.

releasedFindings: Extremity exam reveals tense, woody swelling of right anterior thigh with severe pain on passive knee flexion and diminished light touch sensation.
Serum Calcium: 6.8 mg/dL (ionized calcium 0.88 mmol/L); Serum Phosphorus: 7.2 mg/dL.
Urine output via Foley catheter is only 15 mL over the first hour.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Right thigh compartment syndrome secondary to crush injury; urgent orthopedic evaluation for compartment pressure measurement and emergent fasciotomy; avoid empiric calcium replacement for asymptomatic hypocalcemia (causes metastatic tissue calcification in rhabdomyolysis), but treat life-threatening hyperkalemia immediately; initiate aggressive isotonic IV crystalloid titration targeting urine output 200-300 mL/hr.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Crush Injury Rhabdomyolysis with Pigment-Induced Acute Tubular Necrosis and Thigh Compartment Syndrome
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Prolonged immobilization leading to massive myonecrosis (CK > 78,000 U/L), myoglobinuria (blood on dipstick without RBCs on microscopy), severe AKI (creatinine 3.8), hyperkalemia (6.6), and anterior thigh compartment syndrome.

clinicalScores.formula: Age + Sex + Etiology + CK + Creatinine + Calcium + Phosphate + Bicarbonate
clinicalScores.expectedResult: High risk for requiring renal replacement therapy or mortality
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires full chemistry profile including electrolytes and CK.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Quantify muscle breakdown, renal function, potassium, and calcium/phosphate.

immediateInterventions: IV Calcium Gluconate 10% (10-20 mL) for cardiac membrane stabilization due to K 6.6 with peaked T waves
Insulin 10 units IV + D50W 50 mL for potassium shift
Aggressive IV isotonic saline resuscitation targeting urine output 200-300 mL/hr
Immediate orthopedic surgical consult for emergent fasciotomy
definitiveTherapy: Hemodialysis if refractory hyperkalemia or anuria persists

strictContraindications: Routine IV calcium correction for asymptomatic hypocalcemia in rhabdomyolysis
Potassium-containing IV solutions (avoid Lactated Ringer's until hyperkalemia resolves)
NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, or other nephrotoxins
highRiskInteractions: Administering calcium for early hypocalcemia without ECG changes precipitates widespread metastatic calcification in damaged skeletal muscle.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to treat hyperkalemic ECG changes with membrane stabilization before other measures

mandatoryActions: Immediate IV calcium for peaked T waves

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
